Iterative 3D Super-Resolution (I3DS) is a two-stage alternating training framework designed to super-resolve Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) by disentangling 2D image upscaling from 3D NeRF synchronization [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly defines I3DS as a 'two-stage alternating training framework' that 'disentangles upscaling and NeRF synchronization'. It details Stage 1 as upscaling 2D NeRF renders (using RSD with SD×4) and Stage 2 as synchronizing/updating the 3D NeRF representation using those upscaled images. The claim's description of the purpose (super-resolving NeRFs by disentangling 2D upscaling from 3D synchronization) matches the source's explanation of resolving cross-view inconsistency and achieving detail convergence.

- **When to use**: When high-resolution, view-consistent NeRF reconstruction is required from low-resolution inputs, and direct score distillation methods fail to converge on detailed reconstructions [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that 'directly applying SDS on NeRF renders produces blurred details and would fail to converge on detailed reconstructions' because the supervision is limited to local patches. It further introduces the I3DS framework, which is a two-stage alternating process (Upscaling and Synchronization) designed to solve cross-view inconsistency and achieve high-resolution, view-consistent NeRF reconstruction from low-resolution inputs.
